'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Gaza war]]
**[[Calls for a ceasefire during the Gaza war]]
***The [[United States]] [[United Nations Security Council veto power|vetoes]] a [[United Nations Security Council]] proposal for a [[ceasefire]] in [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]], citing the proposal's not linking the ceasefire to the return of [[Israel–Hamas war hostage crisis|hostages taken during the conflict]]. [https://www.nysun.com/article/america-vetoes-proposed-un-resolution-to-end-gaza-war-which-was-seen-as-betrayal-of-hostages-held-by-hamas (''The New York Sun'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/us-will-veto-un-security-council-resolution-gaza-war-its-current-form-says-2024-11-20/ (Reuters)]
**[[United States support for Israel in the Gaza war]]
***The [[United States Senate]] rejects three resolutions by [[US Senate|senator]] [[Bernie Sanders]] that would block the sale of weapons to [[Israel]] in their war in Gaza. [https://thehill.com/homenews/senate/5001339-senate-rejects-sanders-israel-weapons-resolution/ (''The Hill'')]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[United Kingdom and the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***[[United Kingdom|British]]-produced [[Storm Shadow]] [[cruise missile]]s are launched into [[Russia]]n territory by [[Ukraine]] for the first time, following approval by the [[Starmer ministry|Starmer cabinet]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2024/nov/20/russia-ukraine-war-live-biden-us-weapons-missiles-putin-nuclear?filterKeyEvents=false&page=with%3Ablock-673dfb778f08b8d1c90a6954#block-673dfb778f08b8d1c90a6954 (''The Guardian'')]
**The [[Federal government of the United States|U.S.]], [[Government of Italy|Italian]], [[Government of Greece|Greek]], and [[Government of Spain|Spanish governments]] temporarily close their [[Diplomatic mission|embassies]] in [[Kyiv]], Ukraine, following threats of a "significant air attack" from [[Russian Armed Forces|Russia]]. [https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2024/nov/20/u-allies-shutter-embassies-ukraine-following-threa/ (''The Washington Times'')]
**The embassies of [[Kazakhstan]] and [[Kyrgyzstan]] urge their citizens to leave areas near Ukrainian combat zones or to leave Ukraine altogether amid an escalating risk of Russian retaliatory attacks. [https://timesca.com/war-in-ukraine-kazakhstan-kyrgyzstan-tell-citizens-to-step-up-safety/ (''The Times of Central Asia'')]
*[[Mali War]]
**[[Fall of Timbuktu]]
***The [[International Criminal Court]] sentences [[Mali]]an [[Islamist insurgency in the Sahel|Islamist]] militant and [[Ansar Dine]] member [[al-Hassan Ag Abdoul Aziz]] to 10 years in prison on charges of [[war crime]]s and [[crimes against humanity]] committed in 2012 and 2013 in [[Timbuktu]], Mali. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/11/20/icc-sentences-al-hassan-ag-abdoul-aziz-to-10-years-over-mali-war-crimes (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Battle of Khartoum (2023–2025)|Battle of Khartoum]]
***The [[Sudanese Armed Forces]] intensify their offensive in the [[Khartoum]] capital region, particularly in [[Khartoum North]] where the battle has rapidly escalated. [https://sudantribune.com/article293602/ (Sudan Tribune)]
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**[[Israel's role in the Syrian civil war]]
***Thirty-six people are killed and more than 50 others are injured in [[Israel]]i [[airstrike]]s in [[Palmyra]], [[Syria]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israel-attacks-syrias-palmyra-syrian-state-news-agency-says-2024-11-20/ (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[German economic crisis (2022–present)|German economic crisis]]
**[[U.S.|American]] [[automotive industry|automaker]] [[Ford Motor Company|Ford]] announces that it will cut 4,000 jobs in [[European Union|Europe]], including 2,900 in [[Germany]], citing economic instability and conflicts with [[Environmental law|environmental regulations]]. [https://www.newsweek.com/ford-european-job-cuts-eletric-vehicle-market-1989024 (''Newsweek'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[November 2024 Northeast Pacific bomb cyclone]]
**Two people are killed and more than 570,000 people are [[power outage|without power]] when a [[Explosive cyclogenesis|bomb cyclone]] makes landfall over the [[West Coast of the United States|West Coast]] of the [[United States]] and [[British Columbia]], [[Canada]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2024/11/20/weather/bomb-cylone-west-coast-washington-climate/index.html (CNN)] [https://www.nbcnews.com/weather/winter-weather/bomb-cyclone-pacific-northwest-rcna180941 (NBC News)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2024 Baltic Sea submarine cable disruptions]]
**The [[Government of Russia|Russian government]] denies accusations made by European governments of their involvement in sabotaging two [[Submarine communications cable|submarine telecommunications cables]] in the [[Baltic Sea]] as a means of [[hybrid warfare]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/russia-denies-cutting-baltic-sea-cables-as-tensions-rise/a-70832595 (DW)]
**The [[Royal Danish Navy]] boards the [[China|Chinese]] [[cargo ship]] ''Yi Peng 3'' in the [[Baltic Sea]] after the ship is suspected to be involved in the [[sabotage]] of the submarine cables. [https://eadaily.com/en/news/2024/11/20/the-danish-navy-boarded-a-chinese-cargo-ship-who-broke-the-cables-at-the-bottom-of-the-baltic-sea (EurAsia Daily)]
*[[Capital punishment in Indonesia]]
**[[President of the Philippines|Philippine President]] [[Bongbong Marcos]] confirms the return of [[Mary Jane Veloso]] to the [[Philippines]] following 14 years on [[death row]] in [[Indonesia]], after the [[government of Indonesia|Indonesian government]] implemented a policy for the [[repatriation]] of foreign prisoners. [https://www.scmp.com/week-asia/politics/article/3287274/indonesia-agrees-return-filipino-death-row-inmate-mary-jane-veloso-philippines (''South China Morning Post'')]
*[[India]]n billionaire and [[Adani Group]] chairman [[Gautam Adani]] is indicted in the [[U.S.]] for his role in an alleged multi-billion dollar [[bribery]] and [[fraud]] scheme where he and seven others paid [[Government of India|Indian government]] officials [[US$]]265 million to obtain contracts for [[Adani Green Energy]]. [https://www.asiaone.com/world/billionaire-gautam-adani-indias-adani-group-charged-us-bribery-fraud (AsiaOne)] [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-11-20/us-prosecutors-indict-gautam-adani-on-bribery-charges (Bloomberg)]
*[[New Zealand]] designates [[Yemen]]'s [[Houthi movement]] and [[Lebanon]]'s [[Hezbollah]] as [[List of designated terrorist groups|terrorist groups]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/new-zealand-designates-houthis-and-entirety-of-hezbollah-as-terror-organizations/ (''The Times of Israel'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2024 United Kingdom farmers' protests]]
**[[Deputy Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Deputy Prime Minister]] [[Angela Rayner]] dismisses concerns brought on by protests in [[London]] from [[Agriculture in the United Kingdom|United Kingdom farmers]] against new agricultural inheritance taxation policies as "[[Fearmongering|scaremongering]]". [https://news.sky.com/story/trump-wins-uk-reaction-starmer-labour-badenoch-tories-politics-live-12593360 (Sky News)]
*[[Mali War]]
**[[Mali]]an [[military junta|junta]] chief [[Assimi Goïta]] dismisses [[Prime Minister of Mali|Prime Minister]] [[Choguel Kokalla Maïga]] for criticizing the junta government's decision to indefinitely postpone a return to civilian rule. [https://www.dw.com/en/mali-junta-chief-sacks-prime-minister/a-70837908 (DW)]
*[[Protests against the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Protests against the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**Around 1,671 [[Anti-war movement|anti-war]] protesters in [[Belarus]] are arrested for showing solidarity with [[Ukraine]] as part of a crackdown on [[Belarusian opposition|opposition]] under [[President of Belarus|President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]]. [https://apnews.com/article/belarus-lukashenko-ukraine-war-russia-crackdown-2d517139f969c07210faa9d1f2d2c99b (AP)]
*[[Iraq]] imposes a two-day nationwide [[curfew]] as it conducts its first national [[census]] since 1987. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/11/20/iraq-conducts-first-national-census-in-nearly-40-years (Al Jazeera)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Discoveries of exoplanets]]
**In a study published by the [[Nature (journal)|Nature]] journal, astronomers announce the discovery of [[IRAS 04125+2902 b]], a newborn [[exoplanet]]. The discovery was made by Madyson Barber, a graduate student at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]]. [https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-08123-3 (''Nature'')] [https://abcnews.go.com/Technology/grad-study-discovers-planet-orbiting-nearby-star-astronomers/story?id=116006890 (ABC News)]
